meta.title: The Lost Necklace
meta.textType: story: who or what is it?

paragraphs: On Wednesday, May made a necklace in her art lesson. It was made of blue and white beads on a long string. The necklace was a gift for her mom. May was very happy with it. Her art teacher liked it very much. After the lesson, she put it in the pocket of her school bag.

After school, May and her brother Pat played badminton on the court. It was next to the school, and many children played there. The sun was warm, and the wind was soft. They played for an hour, and May won two games. Then they walked home to the white house next to the school. They put their bags on the sofa and went to wash their hands. Their mom was at work in the library until six o'clock.

When May came back, she looked in her bag. "Where is my necklace?" she asked. "It is lost!" "Maybe you left it on the court," said Pat. "I will run back and look." He ran to the court, and he looked under the net and next to the wall. Nobody was there, and he could not find the necklace. Pat came home, and he looked very tired.

May searched the whole house. She looked under the sofa, behind the door, and in every room. "It is probably in the garden," said Pat. They looked everywhere, but there was no necklace. "Grandma, have you seen it?" asked May. Grandma shook her head. Then May heard two words from the living room. "Pretty! Pretty!"

Bill, the green parrot, sat on the top shelf of the bookshelf. He likes to take small things, and he repeats words all day. Something blue and white lay next to him. "The necklace!" said May. Pat laughed and said, "He took it from your bag!" Finally, May took the necklace from the shelf. Pat took a photo of Bill and the necklace for May. She gave it to her mom in the evening. "It is lovely," said her mom, and she put it on at once. "Pretty!" said Bill, and everybody laughed.
text.summary: May makes a necklace in art class for her mom, and then she loses it. May and Pat search the court and the whole house, and they find it on a bookshelf next to Bill the parrot.
